title: Surety must be man, yet without our guilt
source_text: VI. Ejusmodi vero vadem hominem quoque esse conveniebat, ut peccatum puniretur in eadem natura in qua patratum fuit; sed hominem non eodem cum caeteris hominibus reatu involutum. Etenim qui pro peccatis propriis mortis & maledictionis in judicio divino reus ipse fuisset, non potuisset ultro poenam eandem pro aliis subire.
pass_a_gloss: It was fitting that such a surety also be a man, so that sin be punished in the same nature in which it was committed; yet a man not involved in the same guilt with other men. For one who was himself liable in the divine judgment to death and curse for his own sins could not freely undergo the same penalty for others.
pass_b_english: The surety must be human—punishment in the nature that sinned—yet not himself under our common guilt.
